paper.title_en: Spinning particle dynamics and ISCO structure around Einstein-Bronnikov regular black holes
paper.abstract_en: We study the equatorial dynamics of spinning test particles in the exterior spacetime of the Einstein-Bronnikov black hole, a solution of nonlinear electrodynamics characterized by a magnetic charge parameter $q_m$. Although the Bronnikov geometry is known to resolve the central curvature singularity, our analysis is confined to the external communication domain ($r > r_+$), where the magnetic charge acts as an effective hair that deforms the strong-field region relative to Schwarzschild. Employing the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we analyze the effective potential, innermost stable circular orbits (ISCO), and bound trajectories in this exterior geometry. The spin-curvature coupling significantly alters the orbital structure: positive spin raises the potential barrier and shifts the ISCO outward, while negative spin lowers it, allowing deeper strong-field penetration. We derive the superluminal bound on the spin, showing that the magnetic charge restricts the admissible spin parameter space in the exterior region, with smaller ISCO radii imposing tighter constraints. Systematic computation of ISCO properties reveals that while both $q_m$ and spin s shift these quantities, the accretion efficiency remains modestly affected. Explicit numerical trajectories confirm that the magnetic charge modifies both the radial extent and periastron precession of bound orbits, introducing distinctive signatures from the Schwarzschild case. Our results highlight the necessity of accounting for particle spin in strong-field tests and establish the Einstein-Bronnikov magnetic charge as a viable phenomenological probe of deviations from general relativity in black hole exteriors, though direct tests of the singularity-resolution mechanism would require analysis of trans-horizon dynamics.
